openQuestions: Which mark treatments — line weight, dot policy, area gradient and opacity, bar radius and gap, stack separators, the highlighted mark — are missing or weak in the 26 forms after the shipped phases 15-19?
Which tooltip, legend and interaction patterns in the reference library improve reading without adding decoration our pointer contract cannot afford?
Which colour and dark-ground changes are defensible by number under the cursor register and its six contrast gates?
Which missing micro-visualisations earn a row in the question-first catalogue, and which findings from angles 1-4 become enforceable corpus-check assertions rather than per-template judgement?

resolvedQuestions.question: Where does our five-part card (headline, subtitle, figure, footer finding, source) read as a template rather than a product, judged against the reference cards' anatomy, typography and spacing?
resolvedQuestions.answer: The furniture is at reference parity (type scale 16/14/12, footer weights, 1px rule, 8px gaps — confirmed at both sources); the divergence is figure aspect (26/26 frames 24.4-55.6% of their 720-unit width, median 43.4%, vs the reference's locked 56.25%), and the product gap is the missing prominent number: a metric+delta register in the header, which every product-grade reference leads with.

keyFindings.title: Our figures run shorter of the reference aspect; the text furniture is at parity
keyFindings.summary: Divergence is the figure, not the furniture; 25/26 frames sit 24-47% width-relative vs their 56.25%.

keyFindings.title: The product gap is the missing prominent number in the header
keyFindings.evidence: daily-line.html:104,227-228; contract type scale; details/apple-hig-charts-light-07/-08, details/vercel-docs-analytics-light-01, tremor-blocks-light.jpg notes
keyFindings.summary: No scalar/time-series form carries its reading as a number; every product-grade reference leads with it.

keyFindings.title: Ours already better: conclusion headlines and jitter-free axis numbers
Header chrome, fixed insets and date-thinned labels are kept differences
keyFindings.summary: Their mechanisms need a runtime; ours need a one-time measurement. No change.

keyFindings.title: The reference's signed trend cue is a 16px inline-SVG icon
keyFindings.summary: A direction cue is available as a hand-drawn 2-path inline mark; feeds the metric+delta shape.

keyFindings.title: The footer text register is at reference parity
keyFindings.summary: The metric+delta work is additive in the header; the footer needs nothing.

ruledOut.approach: Header controls, a header border and fixed 12px insets in every card
ruledOut.reason: Their mechanisms need a runtime and component library; our eight inert forms and widest-label insets are recorded decisions

ruledOut.approach: Changes to card padding, card width or footer weights
ruledOut.reason: Dimension-for-dimension parity with the reference footer confirmed at both sources

ruledOut.approach: Trusting the contract prose over the shipped file for the area fade
ruledOut.reason: The file says 0.35/0.04 where the prose says 0.8/0.1; the discrepancy moved to angle 2's evidence
